messages.subject: Missing Data and item-person ft
parts:
Hi Phil,

i realized that itemfit, personfit and fitIndices are not calculated with missing data.
Is imputation the only way around this?
I am comparing Rasch to other IRT models and have plenty of missing data (the "non-aplicable" response was coded as missing)

Thanks,

Carolina

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Missing Data and item-person ft
parts:
Hi Carolina,

Unfortunately most if not all of fit statistics are ill defined when missing data are present, so complete data is really the only option here. 

However, instead of an imputation approach you could try fitting the data with the missing response data to obtain FIML estimates, create a new smaller dataset which omits the missing response cases, and form a new non-estimated model with the FIML estimated coefficients on the smaller dataset that contains only complete observations. Using this model will allow you to use the functions that you mentioned. I'm not sure how kosher this is in the literature but I think it's justifiable if item, person, and model diagnostics really are important, and at least should give valid results for cases with non-missing data. 

Otherwise if you are just interested in nested model comparisons likelihood ratio tests are still valid, along with their information theoretic counterparts (AIC, BIC, etc.) through the anova() generic. Hope that helps!

Phil
